paper_metadata.title: The Qubit Shift: Unveiling Next-Generation Deep Learning with Quantum Computing

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical deep learning benchmark using variational quantum circuits with amplitude/angle encoding on public benchmark datasets (MNIST, CIFAR-10, S&P 500, QM9) evaluated on IBM Quantum systems and simulators.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid quantum-classical variational quantum circuit deep learning
algorithm.ansatz: Alternating layers of parameterized single-qubit rotations (Ry, Rz, and mentioned Ru) and CNOT entangling layers; hardware-efficient style
algorithm.optimizer: Adam, SGD, and L-BFGS are all mentioned; exact optimizer used per run not specified

hyperparameters.learning_rate: reduced learning rates during joint training; exact value not reported
hyperparameters.entanglement_pattern: nearest-neighbor initially, adaptive long-range additions based on gradient threshold
hyperparameters.training_strategy: staged training: classical components first, then quantum parameters unfrozen

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Amplitude encoding is used for dense feature vectors with log2(N) qubits for N-dimensional vectors; angle encoding maps classical features to Ry rotation angles. The paper also gives an illustrative feature-encoding algorithm using Ry(arcsin(x_norm[i])) and controlled rotations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Not explicitly formulated; generic supervised learning objective implied by minimizing a cost function via classical optimization of quantum circuit parameters

problem_instance.description: Benchmark evaluations on image classification and regression tasks: MNIST, CIFAR-10, S&P 500, and QM9.

dataset_specification.MNIST: 70,000 samples, 784 features, 10 classes, amplitude encoding, 10 qubits
dataset_specification.CIFAR-10: 60,000 samples, 3,072 features, 10 classes, angle encoding, 12 qubits
dataset_specification.S&P 500: 100,000 samples, 50 features, regression, amplitude encoding, 6 qubits
dataset_specification.QM9: 134,000 samples, 29 features, regression, hybrid encoding, 8 qubits

data_preprocessing_details: Normalize feature vector x to x_norm = x / ||x|| for amplitude encoding
Use arcsin(x_norm[i]) for Ry feature mapping in the illustrative encoding algorithm
Fixed random seeds and standardized initialization procedures
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Benchmarking across multiple datasets; comparative analysis against classical counterparts; hardware and simulator runs; no explicit cross-validation or number of independent runs reported

noise_model.mitigation_details: Results from circuits with artificially increased noise are extrapolated to the zero-noise limit; known error channels are compensated via quasi-probability decomposition; idle periods use dynamical decoupling; conservation-law checks used for symmetry verification
classical_preprocessing: Staged training with classical layers trained first
classical_postprocessing: Accuracy and training-time comparison against classical baselines

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Training convergence shown for CIFAR-10, but numeric curve data not reported

speedup_claims.conditions: Across multiple benchmark datasets; staged training with quantum parameters unfrozen after classical components
speedup_claims.caveats: No absolute training times reported; exact per-dataset timing and run counts not specified.
The paper reports 1,250 parameters for the hybrid model versus 25,000 for the classical network; no uncertainty or multiple-run statistics reported.
